tagline: Boat-only access to a protected Red Sea national park — the same near-monopoly logic as Giftun.
summary: Marsa Alam is the southern Red Sea's remote, pristine resort coast, and its marquee waterborne draw is Wadi El Gemal National Park: the Qulaan/Hamata island archipelago (Siyul, Showarit, Um El Sheikh), reachable only by boat from Hamata Marina. This is the same boat-only, near-monopoly access pattern that anchors the Giftun corridors up the coast at Hurghada — a strong candidate for economics once park-permit and operator volumes are pinned.

seasonality: Red Sea is warm and diveable year-round; summer heat is extreme. Southern reef waters are generally calm.
